sections.title: Jehoshaphat's Reign Begins
observations: Jehoshaphat, the son of Asa, ascends to the throne of Judah and begins his reign with a commitment to follow the ways of the Lord, unlike the kings of Israel.
He removes the high places and Asherah poles, which were remnants of idolatry, indicating a desire to purify worship in Judah.

sections.title: Seeking the Lord
observations: Jehoshaphat actively seeks the Lord and encourages the people of Judah to do the same, sending officials to teach the Law of the Lord throughout the cities.
This emphasis on teaching and returning to the covenant relationship with God is a hallmark of his leadership.

sections.title: Military Strength and Alliances
observations: As a result of his faithfulness, Jehoshaphat's kingdom experiences peace and prosperity. He builds a strong military and fortifies cities, preparing for potential threats.
His alliances with Israel through marriage highlight the complexities of political relationships in the ancient Near East.

importantVerses.commentary: The Lord was with Jehoshaphat because he walked in the earlier ways of his father David and did not seek the Baals.
They taught in Judah, having the Book of the Law of the Lord with them; they went about through all the cities of Judah and taught among the people.
These were the servants of the king, besides those whom the king put in the fortified cities throughout all Judah.

questions: What does Jehoshaphat's commitment to remove idolatry teach us about the importance of purity in worship?
How can we apply the principle of seeking the Lord and teaching His Word in our own communities today?
What lessons can be learned from Jehoshaphat's military preparations and alliances in relation to our spiritual battles?
